features.notes: Native compatibility remains unproven outside the documented fixture matrix. Darwin standalone access-time evidence covers 216 Mach-O cases plus 168 bundle read-only controls and 80 DMG cases using released APFS v0.9.0. Signing/removal/dry runs refresh Mach-O source access and give replacements a later access time; display/verification preserve executable stat metadata. DMG access is preserved; all 80 DMG metadata cases now match bytes, including twenty native in-place dry runs delivered in PR #49. ACL inheritance and wider metadata profiles remain open.

Native compatibility remains unproven outside the documented fixture matrix. The readable/searchable executable-directory profile adds 624 POSIX comparisons across three architectures, seven operand/tree shapes and independent directory/file modes. Mach-O dry runs check allocation and discard it without restoring metadata. Allocation permission failures retain independent sibling commits and the affected bundle envelope, preserve its executable/sidecars and skip ancestor writes. Windows uses real DACL-denial unit tests. Bundle source access is recorded at allocation rather than planning: the 624 directory cases require read-access parity for dispatched work, including shallow descendants and allocation-blocked ancestors. Native exception-aware scheduling can leave independent siblings entirely unstarted; explicit member manifests verify those unchanged subtrees and record the difference from Go sibling completion. Another 252 native cases cover selective signing and already-signed rejection across seven layouts; 54 failure-boundary cases cover envelope/cleanup failures, including 18 combinations with allocation denial. Source access is deferred until execution reaches the executable; envelope failures leave their executable unread and child-cleanup failures leave ancestors unread. APFS v0.9.0 CopyAccessTime copies the deferred source read into the private staged replacement with exact Darwin precision. Preparation-error preservation, source/staging identity and cancellation remain covered. All 54 failure-boundary cases require matching source and replacement access. Deep dry runs allocate reached unsigned children before unchanged on-disk seals fail. Another 72 native cases cover helpers, child bundles and grandchildren, three architectures, past/future access, deep/force/shallow operations and allocation denial. Twelve portable cases cover allocation-error precedence and cancellation without byte/envelope commits. This single-chain corpus does not establish arbitrary planning failure or asynchronous sibling parity. Replacement access is refreshed after successful signature cleanup, with root-relative committed-inode checks. A 504-case native matrix covers stale directory/symlink failures across seven layouts, three architectures, past/future access, unsigned/signed/read-only signing, signed/unsigned removal and dry runs. Inaccessible directories, broader asynchronous failures, other filesystems and raw diagnostic parity remain open.

Default Current and explicit physical version selection support signing, display, verification and removal. Nested verification checks every physical version against the parent's requirement; deep checks include pages/resources/descendants. Twelve native selected-signing tree comparisons, 90 display cases, six removal comparisons, 21 shallow/deep cases and three native fixtures establish the bounded profile. Direct physical/Current version directories are supported as standalone bundles and reject additional selectors, with 64 native failure/preservation comparisons. Contents parents ignore selection and children use their own Current. Wider discovery, malformed-selector diagnostics and complete option interactions remain incomplete.
Must be implemented and independently verified before full-parity release.

Re-signing preserves existing trailing allocation bytes. Darwin requires clone support and rejects protected/compressed files; wider metadata, bundle symlink and filesystem support remains incomplete. Display exports owned DER from supported CMS metadata in leaf-first order, including an embedded root. Optional attached/default/empty prefixes, shared architecture selection, overwrite/link/stale-file behavior, partial failures, multiple targets and ignored sign/verify/remove applicability have 115 portable and two Mac cases. Extraction does not establish integrity or trust; modified pages still extract and unreadable CMS yields no files. Broader CMS/chains, native host-chain augmentation, signature slots, detached/generic representations, output aliases to inputs and full error/option interactions remain incomplete. Existing bundle-parent alias paths and combined entitlement display retain explicit diagnostic differences.

RFC 3161 verification, separate explicit TSA roots, historical certificate validity, library timestamp providers and nonce-bound SHA-256 exchanges are implemented. A public-test RSA arm64 signature exactly replays a recorded native Apple token; Apple and OpenSSL acceptance are exercised. The CLI signs with online HTTP --timestamp[=URL], verifies and displays timestamps, and supports --timestamp=none. Bundled Apple roots are explicit TSA inputs. A bounded pure-Go HTTP transport is exercised against a local authority on all targets; opt-in live Apple acceptance covers three Mach-O forms. Full TSA/Apple policy, proxy/redirect behavior, revocation, general CMS/BER and localized dates remain incomplete.

RSA/ECDSA PEM and authenticated PKCS#12 signing, native allocation, Apple BER CMS/hash agility, leaf pins and portable explicit-CA chain policy are implemented. The existing 64-case matrix is supplemented by three organization-anchor comparisons, a Developer ID csreq comparison, 24 native PKCS#12 signatures and real public Developer ID chain/Team ID checks. Authorities, fixed-format signing-time and RFC 3161 timestamp metadata are displayed. Timestamp callbacks and separate TSA trust add native replay evidence. Full PKIX/Apple policy, localized dates, end-to-end Developer ID signing, broader TSA transport policy, hybrid algorithms and revocation remain incomplete.

APPL/BNDL/XPC! Contents layouts and unversioned/multiple-version FMWK frameworks support XML/binary metadata, resources, nested code, signing, inspection, verification and outer-only removal. Explicit selection preserves other versions; nested verification applies the parent's requirement to every physical version. Direct physical/Current directories use independent resource boundaries and canonical display paths. Main-executable paths and file aliases select supported bundles by resolved filename; helpers and hard-link aliases remain standalone. Framework executable aliases select the physical version and reject further selection. Mach-O bundle writes now stage root-relative APFS replacements, preserving external hard-link neighbours; resource envelopes retain in-place/unlink semantics. The 126-case writer matrix compares complete native trees and inode effects; native executable ACL inheritance, uncovered access-time profiles and failure-diagnostic parity remain incomplete. The bounded Darwin executable access-time profile adds 294 comparisons for signing, re-signing, outer removal and dry runs, with source hard-link observations, later replacement access and untouched removal descendants. The read-access API from merged APFS PR #110 is released in v0.8.0 and retained in v0.9.0, without a local module replacement or workspace. Final per-commit codesign CI and artifact evidence is recorded in the implementation PR. Display/verification, standalone files, envelope/resource access times and broader failure/permission profiles remain outside this bounded claim. The Darwin creation-time profile adds 210 native comparisons and sets only staged bundle executables to a new time capped by the source modification time. The setter was released in APFS v0.7.0 from merged PR #108 and is retained in the v0.9.0 pin. Linux/Windows retain their existing replacement metadata policy; the new creation-time corpus runs only on Darwin. New signature directories copy canonical bundle-root stat metadata through APFS v0.6.0, with selected physical framework roots and unchanged existing directories. Forty directory cases and eight native security profiles cover the bounded stat profile; explicit source ACL copying and subsequent envelope inheritance remain incomplete. Regular stale signature files are purged after each rewritten main executable; removal empties only the selected signature directory and dry runs retain sidecars. A 105-case native matrix covers regular cleanup and external links. Another 210 native cases and four nested failure cases cover stale directories and internal/dangling/outside symlinks: cleanup rejects them after executable replacement, dry-run signing preserves them and succeeds, and a child failure stops the parent commit. A further 278 native comparisons cover case-insensitive APFS ASCII cleanup order, including hash collisions and entries before CodeResources. Removal rejects non-regular CodeResources after executable replacement when enumeration reaches it. Signing rejects envelope directories at their write, retaining earlier child commits and preserving dry-run trees. Signing/removal skip unused old child-envelope reads, permitting write-only POSIX envelopes; required verification reads remain. Another 104 portable directory/commit-order cases and 20 POSIX permission cases cover this profile. Windows explicitly skips POSIX permission probes. Symlinked signing envelopes retain early rejection. PR #34 merged this ordering slice with APFS v0.6.0. Merged PR #35 pins released v0.6.1, including APFS PR #106's public hashing API first-use race fix published through release PR #107. Its final three-OS, packaging, race/fuzz, native-import and artifact checks passed with that released dependency; the actual merge matches the audited tree recorded in docs/implementation_plan.md. Bounded metadata traversal and internal write-alias rejection remain; other filesystem orders, special files, unreadable subtrees, broader permissions and raw diagnostics remain incomplete. Malformed/oversized/symlinked metadata retains stricter rejection. Relative existing resource links use symlink text seals. Staged signing constructs the complete tree before writes, with shared bounds and cross-bundle/version hard-link checks within the selected boundary. Native comparisons, mutations, Clang AST records and six fixture sets establish the bounded profile. Each Linux/Windows producer exports 45 prior app artifacts plus 63 layout archives, nine multi-version trees, nine direct-path trees, nine executable-path trees, 84 writer archives and 42 cleanup archives for native strict deep verification. Broader symlink/xattr policy, discovery, custom rules and full strict/diagnostic parity remain incomplete. See docs/bundles.md for limits. A pinned direct go-apfs-v2/pkg/disk dependency supplies DMGFooter. Single-segment UDIF v4 signing, inspection and verification preserve payload bytes and bind the canonical trailer in slot 6. Forty ad-hoc native byte/display comparisons, fifteen ad-hoc/RSA/P-256 native signature and hdiutil checks, five native fixtures, matched-time RSA equality, local TSA tests and a live Apple timestamp establish the tested profile. Ad-hoc path dry runs now flush requirements/empty CMS and optional entitlements without a CodeDirectory, leaving an unsigned image in place. Seventy lifecycle cases, four native permission cases and all 80 access/metadata comparisons cover the bounded profile; CI compares 140 foreign dry-run images independently. SignBytes remains construction-only. Certificate path dry runs return unsupported instead of reproducing the recorded native memory faults; the bounded replacement notice now matches for supported inputs. Native-unsupported removal preserves input. Encrypted/segmented images, streaming, detached signatures, additional digests, notarization policy and full option/diagnostic parity remain incomplete.
